topPRs.title: op-reth: test the proofs RPC window edges and old-block witness requests
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
The historical-proofs RPC handler (`rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/proofs.rs`) and its state-provider factory (`state.rs`) had no tests, and the only e2e check near the window's earliest block was the dormant `proofs/prune` package. The reth 2.6 bump (#23046) rewrites the handler, so this pins what `eth_getProof`, `debug_executePayload` and `debug_executionWitness` answer at and around the window's edges before the rewrite lands.

## What the tests cover

### Rust: `OpStateProviderFactory::state_provider` (`rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/state.rs`, 16 cases)

A mock eth API (`reth_rpc::EthApi` over `MockEthProvider`) with a canonical chain of 21 blocks and an `InMemoryProofsStorage` seeded with blocks 10..=18, so the store trails the head the way it does between flushes:

- served: the earliest block (by number and by hash), a block inside the window, the latest stored block (by number and by hash)
- refused with `StateForNumberNotFound(n)`: one below the earliest (by number and by hash of the canonical block), genesis, one above the store tip, the chain head the store has not flushed, the `latest` tag while the store trails
- served once the store holds the head: the `latest` tag, no block id, the head by number
- an unknown hash is `ProviderError::Other("header not found")` (the wrapping that ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#474 reports as surfacing to clients as an internal error)
- an empty store refuses everything

Not covered in Rust: a hash that names a known non-canonical block. `MockEthProvider` resolves `block_number(hash)` and `block_hash(number)` from the same header map, so a non-canonical block cannot be modelled; the e2e reorg check below covers that branch.

The test build enables `reth-optimism-trie/metrics` so `OpProofsStorage<S>` is the production wrapper, as it is for the node and for CI's `--workspace --all-features` clippy and nextest runs; without it the alias is the bare `S` and clippy flags the conversion the node needs.

### e2e, in `rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/core` (CI job `op-reth-e2e-sysgo-tests`, `just test-e2e-sysgo` with the default `GO_PKG_NAME=proofs/core`)

`TestProofsFollowerServesExactlyTheWindowItReports`, matrix threshold {7, 50} x proofs path {index, execute}, each cell a sequencer without proofs history (the independent `eth_getProof` reference, `--rpc.eth-proof-window`) and a follower with a 20-block window, `--rpc.max-tracing-requests=2`, 1s blocks. The chain is driven past the window until pruning ran, then sequencing is stopped so the window stands still, and the cell checks:

- the earliest block is served by number and by hash, verifies against the header and matches the reference; the chain is driven a window past the workload's setup block first, so the earliest block holds the workload's accounts
- one below the earliest is refused by number and by hash with an error naming the block (develop: `no state found for block number N`)
- the latest block is served by number, by hash and by the `latest` tag and equals the reference at the head
- `eth_getProof` latency at the earliest block versus the latest (medians of 10), logged for the bump comparison and bounded at 10x with a 250ms floor so only a lookup that re-walks the window can trip it
- `debug_executePayload` builds on the earliest block
- `debug_executionWitness` refuses the earliest block (it executes on the parent's state, which pruning removed) and serves the block after it
- 8 concurrent `debug_executionWitness` requests, above the 2 tracing permits and above the handler's own 3, all succeed
- after sequencing resumes, the first new height is refused until `debug_proofsSyncStatus` reports it and never answered with a proof of another block, then matches the reference; the subtest stops the chain again, so every subtest starts from a stopped chain and can run alone
- a block the test sequencer builds on the head and then replaces: its hash is refused once the follower reorged, the replacement is served by hash and matches the reference

`TestProofsFollowerServesBlocksBelowRethHistoryPruneCheckpoint`, threshold {7, 50}, index path: the follower's reth prunes account and storage history 5 blocks behind its persisted tip (through a `--config` file, since reth's unwind-safe minimum of 10064 blocks has to be lowered in the file and `--prune.*` flags replace the file's prune section), with a proofs window that reaches below that checkpoint. Once `eth_getStorageAt` at the window's earliest block reports reth's own state as pruned, `eth_getProof` there must verify and match the reference and `debug_executionWitness` for the next block must execute: the store serves the window, not reth's history. This is the "block below reth's history prune checkpoint" cell from the issue; the issue's `--full` flag cannot be used because it pins the history distance to 10064 blocks.

The dormant `proofs/prune` package is folded into these checks (window read from `debug_proofsSyncStatus` and asserted equal to the configured window after pruning, pruned block refused, new earliest served) and deleted.

## Matrix

| test | threshold | proofs path | state masking |
|---|---|---|---|
| window edges | 7, 50 | index, execute | 0 only (develop compiles masking out; #23046 rejects a nonzero value; ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#457) |
| history-pruned follower | 7, 50 | index | 0 |

L2 CL is op-node in every cell: the suite's preset runs op-node and the reorg check drives op-node's test sequencer.

## Local verification

Rust (`cd rust && cargo test -p reth-optimism-rpc --lib state::`): 17 passed. `cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-rpc --all-targets` clean, `just fmt-check` clean.

e2e, run from `rust/op-reth/tests` against a debug op-reth built from this worktree (copied out of the shared target dir and selected with `RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH`, with the recipe's other env vars set by hand because `just test-e2e-sysgo` hard-codes `../../target/release/op-reth`, which has no release build here):

```
DISABLE_OP_E2E_LEGACY=true DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo OP_RETH_ENABLE_PROOF_HISTORY=true RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<debug op-reth> \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -v -run 'TestProofsFollowerServesExactlyTheWindowItReports/<cell>$' ./proofs/core/
```

| cell | result | setup block | window after pruning | pruned block refused with | eth_getProof median latency earliest / latest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-index | PASS (85s) | 18 | [29, 49] | `no state found for block number 28` | 455µs / 406µs |
| threshold_7-execute | PASS (85s) | 18 | [28, 48] | `no state found for block number 27` | 418µs / 346µs |
| threshold_50-index | PASS (84s) | 18 | [27, 47] | `no state found for block number 26` | 351µs / 302µs |
| threshold_50-execute | PASS (85s) | 18 | [28, 48] | `no state found for block number 27` | 417µs / 370µs |

Every cell: `debug_executionWitness` for the earliest block is refused naming the block below it; the height imported right after sequencing resumed was refused with `no state found for block number N` while `debug_proofsSyncStatus` still reported the previous head, then matched the reference once flushed; the reorged-out hash was refused with `header not found` and the replacement served once the store had indexed blocks above it. The stale-proof probe right after the reorg (see Findings) reported `stale=true` in threshold_7-index and threshold_7-execute and `stale=false` in threshold_50-index and threshold_50-execute.

`TestProofsFollowerServesBlocksBelowRethHistoryPruneCheckpoint` (same env, `-run 'TestProofsFollowerServesBlocksBelowRethHistoryPruneCheckpoint'`):

| cell | result | chain head at the stop | reth history probe (block: state) | checked block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7 | PASS (72s) | 65 | 1, 14, 27, 28 all `pruned` | 28 served from the store, witness for 29 executes |
| threshold_50 | PASS (112s) | 105 | 1, 14, 27, 28 all `pruned` | 28 served from the store, witness for 29 executes |

Not run locally: op-geth validator (`OP_DEVSTACK_PROOF_VALIDATOR_EL=op-geth` skips both tests with a message) and a kona-node CL (the preset runs op-node).

## Findings

- **Stale proofs right after a same-height reorg (bug candidate).** Once the follower's reth has adopted a replacement block at a height the proofs store already holds, and until the ExEx has processed the reorg notification, `eth_getProof` by the replacement's hash passes the canonical-hash check and the window check and answers with the replaced block's state. `debug_proofsSyncStatus` cannot reveal the gap: it reports numbers, and the height is "served". Reproduced once in a local run of the reorg subtest (threshold 7, index path): 2ms after the follower reported the reorg at height 59, the window was still `[39, 59]` and the proof for the recorder at 59 failed with `block 59 account 0x49C0...: eth_getProof from validator does not verify against state root 0xd97c...`. The store's `ProofWindowRange.latest` carries the hash of the stored tip, so the factory could refuse requests while that hash is not the canonical hash of the height (or, for deeper reorgs, while the store's tip is on the replaced chain). The subtest now records whether it hit the gap and waits for the store to index blocks above the replacement before asserting; a fix should turn that probe into an assertion.
- `debug_executionWitness` cannot serve the window's earliest block: it executes the block on its parent's state, which is the state pruning removed, so it fails with `no state found for block number <earliest-1>`. The oldest block whose witness a proofs node serves is earliest+1; `debug_executePayload` on the earliest block works. kona-host callers that walk down to `debug_proofsSyncStatus.earliest` should stop one block above it. Recorded, not a bug in the handler.
- On develop, eth_getProof answers from the proofs store even where reth's own history is pruned: with account and storage history pruned before block 30, reth refuses `eth_getStorageAt` at 28 and below while the proofs follower serves verified proofs there and executes the witness for 29. The "broader limitation" paragraph of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#474 (the path "fails on a history-pruned reth even when the proofs store has the block") does not reproduce on develop: `state_at_block_id` only builds a lazy historical provider, and the overlay reads accounts, storage and trie nodes from the store, reth only for bytecode and block hashes. The bump's rewrite can be checked against this test.
- reth still answers historical state at the prune target block itself (`before = 30` leaves 29 served, 28 refused): reconstructing state at the target needs only the changesets above it. The test checks the block below the target.
- reth refuses a history prune distance under its unwind-safe minimum of 10064 blocks in both the CLI and the config file, and `full` is rejected the same way, so the issue's `--full` follower cannot be built on a short chain. A `before = <block>` mode in the config file with `minimum_pruning_distance` lowered in the same file is accepted; `--prune.*` flags cannot be used alongside, since they replace the file's prune section and with it the lowered minimum.
- The pruner's own decisions are only logged at debug and the devstack prints op-reth's log at the test level, so the history-pruned follower runs with `--log.stdout.filter=info,pruner=debug,engine::persistence=debug` and the test keeps `RecordLogLines` records of the pruner's runs, which it prints when the precondition fails.
- The error a client gets for a block outside the window on develop is `no state found for block number N` (an internal error, as #474 notes); the tests assert the error names the block, not its wording, so the bump can change the message.
- The `latest` tag on a proofs follower resolves to the chain head and is refused while the store trails it (the Rust case `latest_tag_while_the_store_trails`); the e2e `latest` check runs with the chain stopped so the store has caught up.

## Seams

- `utils.NewMixedOpProofPreset(t, opts...)` takes `MixedOpProofPresetConfig` options: deployer options and per-node op-reth options for the sequencer and the validator, so a core test can run the reference-sequencer pattern of the acceptance tests.
- `utils.ValidatorELKind(t)` for skipping when `OP_DEVSTACK_PROOF_VALIDATOR_EL` is not op-reth.
- `utils.NextPayloadAttributes(parent, rawTxs...)` and `utils.SignedTransfer(...)` replace the attribute construction the two `debug_executePayload` tests duplicated.

Stacked on #23429, #23428, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23390

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack,op-reth: hold the sequencer to its block schedule across persistence runs
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Nothing held an op-reth sequencer to its block schedule across reth's persistence runs: the fork fix reth#26708 existed because persistence stalled payload building, and the reth 2.6 bump (#23046) replaces that mechanism with upstream's overlay snapshots, makes persistence batches about seven times larger (threshold 7 to 50) and deletes the fork's regression test `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/payload_handoff.rs`. This adds an acceptance test that keeps a sequencer under load for at least three persistence runs and fails on the first missed slot, and a node-level test that stalls a persistence batch inside the database and requires the next payload job to finish within the block time, written against hooks that survive the bump.

## What the tests cover

### `op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_sequencer_persistence`

`TestOpRethSequencerKeepsScheduleAcrossPersistenceRuns`: an op-reth sequencer alone (no proofs history, so reth's persistence is the only one on it) on `--engine.persistence-threshold={7,50}` with `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target=5` and 1s blocks, with the batcher the mixed runtime attaches. A package-local workload keeps it under load from two accounts off the test goroutine, in rounds of 8 transactions submitted back to back with the last one awaited: either transfers between the accounts, or calls to a contract that creates 16 storage slots it has never written per call (`dsl.EOA.DeployStorageFiller`), so every persistence run writes a batch of new state. The test holds the sequencer to its schedule for three times the threshold in blocks through the new `dsl.L2ELNode.AdvancedOnSchedule` wait, stops the load (failing if it had failed first), and requires op-reth to have logged nothing at error level meanwhile (`RecordLogs` from #23427).

Three times the threshold puts at least three persistence runs inside the window wherever it starts: reth persists once more than the threshold of blocks sit in memory and keeps the last 5, so a run starts every threshold+1-5 blocks (at threshold 50 at blocks 51, 97, 143, ...; at threshold 7 every three blocks).

Matrix: threshold {7, 50} x load {transfers, storage_writes} as subtests, CL {op-node, kona-node} through `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND` (CI runs both). Skips on op-geth.

### `dsl.L2ELNode.AdvancedOnSchedule(blocks, blockTime)`

Waits for the unsafe head to be on schedule (a sequencer that starts behind its genesis time builds back-to-back blocks until it has caught up, bounded by `ScheduleOpts.CatchUpTimeout`), then samples the head eight times per block time until it has advanced `blocks` blocks, and fails as soon as a slot is missed: every new block must extend the previous head, carry the previous head's timestamp plus the block time, and be seen canonical before its own timestamp plus the block time has passed on the wall clock, which is when the next block is due; a block not seen within a further block time of being due fails the wait before it arrives. The pure check `blockOnSchedule` has a table test. The wait logs the largest lag it saw.

### `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/payload_during_persistence.rs`

`payload_job_completes_while_persistence_batch_is_in_flight`, an `rstest` table over threshold {7, 50} (reth 2.5's and 2.6's defaults). It launches the op-reth node on a `WriteGatedDatabase`, a `Database` wrapper injected through `NodeBuilder::with_database` that delegates everything and parks every write transaction at a gate right after opening it while the gate is closed. reth's persistence service opens its write transaction (`database_provider_rw`) before it writes anything in `on_save_blocks`, so closing the gate right before a batch is due keeps that batch in flight inside its transaction with nothing committed, and the test decides when it lands. The scenario, through the engine API like a consensus client (forkchoiceUpdated with attributes, engine_getPayloadV3, engine_newPayloadV3, forkchoiceUpdated):

1. Build `threshold` blocks; nothing is on disk yet.
2. Close the gate and build one more block, which with `memory_block_buffer_target = 0` makes reth persist the whole chain as one batch; wait for the persistence service to be parked.
3. Start a payload job and require it to resolve within 2s (OP Mainnet's block time) with the batch still parked, and the disk still at genesis.
4. Start another payload job with the batch parked, then release the batch while the job runs and wait for it to reach the disk. Send a transfer to the pool, wait for the job's best payload to be rebuilt with it (so the rebuild read state after the batch landed), and require the job to resolve within 2s and its payload to be valid under newPayload, which checks the state root the builder computed across the batch's landing. Then wait for the in-memory state to drop the batch.
5. Build one more block on the persisted base.

A guard opens the gate when dropped, so a failed assertion cannot leave the persistence service parked through shutdown. Every engine call and wait is bounded at 20s with a message naming the stalled step.

The deleted `payload_handoff.rs` tested the fork's mechanism (`suppress_persistence_during_build`, the deferred persisted handoff, the persistence-completion metric), none of which exists after the bump. The replacement uses only `NodeBuilder::with_database`, the `Database` trait, `PayloadBuilderHandle::best_payload` and the in-memory state's persisted marker, all unchanged on the #23046 pin (reth rev 8d359d0), so it is the regression test that carries over. Step 4 is the window the fork protected (a batch landing while a job holds the old overlay) and the one 2.6 changes (the job keeps its own snapshot and persistence reclaims the overlay at once), covered the same way on both.

## Local verification

Run with this tree's debug op-reth (built by the previous agent of the stack from the same Rust tree) and the kona-node release copied out of the shared cargo target, contracts prebuilt:

```
RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<copy of rust/target/debug/op-reth> RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_NODE=<copy of rust/target/release/kona-node> \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 30m -parallel 2 -run 'TestOpRethSequencerKeepsScheduleAcrossPersistenceRuns' -v ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_sequencer_persistence/
```

op-node (default), all four cells pass, 234s for the package at `-parallel 2` (the run of the final code; an earlier run before the review changes passed with the same shape of numbers):

| cell | blocks held to schedule | rounds included (transactions) | largest lag seen | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-transfers | 6 to 27 | 17 (136) | 74ms | 34s |
| threshold_7-storage_writes | 7 to 28 | 18 (144) | 77ms | 35s |
| threshold_50-transfers | 6 to 156 | 130 (1040) | 80ms | 163s |
| threshold_50-storage_writes | 7 to 157 | 132 (1056) | 79ms | 164s |

About seven transactions per block; the threshold-50 storage cell created 16,896 storage slots over 150 blocks, about 5,000 per persistence run. No block was later than half a block time (the wait logs those at warning level) and no op-reth error log in any cell. The runs below were made while cargo builds for this PR ran on the same machine.

With `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node` (kona-node release from this tree's `rust/kona` at the base commit), all four cells pass, 204s for the package (final code; an earlier run before the review changes passed the same way):

| cell | blocks held to schedule | rounds included (transactions) | largest lag seen | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-transfers | 6 to 27 | 17 (136) | 127ms | 38s |
| threshold_7-storage_writes | 7 to 28 | 15 (120) | 118ms | 35s |
| threshold_50-transfers | 6 to 156 | 124 (992) | 175ms | 167s |
| threshold_50-storage_writes | 7 to 157 | 126 (1008) | 128ms | 164s |

No cell needed the catch-up wait under either CL: the workload's setup covered the blocks the sequencer builds back to back after start.

Against #23046's op-reth (reth 2.6.0, built from the bump head 93d9ec9d2f, op-node CL), all four cells pass, 202s for the package:

| cell | blocks held to schedule | rounds included (transactions) | largest lag seen | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-transfers | 10 to 31 | 18 (144) | 76ms | 38s |
| threshold_7-storage_writes | 7 to 28 | 16 (128) | 78ms | 35s |
| threshold_50-transfers | 10 to 160 | 129 (1032) | 92ms | 166s |
| threshold_50-storage_writes | 7 to 157 | 130 (1040) | 92ms | 164s |

So the verification criterion holds on both: no missed slot on `develop` and on #23046, under both thresholds and both loads.

Rust (`cd rust && cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --test it payload_during_persistence`):

```
test payload_during_persistence::payload_job_completes_while_persistence_batch_is_in_flight::case_1_reth_2_5_default ... ok
test payload_during_persistence::payload_job_completes_while_persistence_batch_is_in_flight::case_2_reth_2_6_default ... ok
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 20 filtered out; finished in 2.32s
```

Negative control (not committed): with `config.engine.persistence_backpressure_threshold = Some(persistence_threshold + 1)` the parked batch makes the engine backpressure at the batch tip, and both cases fail as they should with `forkchoice update with attributes stalled` after the 20s call bound, with the gate guard letting the node shut down (43s for both cases, no hang).

`cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-node --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the pinned nightly `just fmt-fix` are clean. (Locally, rustc 1.95 hit an incremental-compilation ICE, "unstable fingerprints for evaluate_obligation", twice while iterating on this test target; `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` sidesteps it and CI builds are not incremental.)

Unit: `go test -run TestBlockOnSchedule ./op-devstack/dsl/` passes.

## Corrections to the issue

- "Assert every block's timestamp delta equals the block time and that no slot is missed": on the OP Stack the timestamp delta alone cannot catch a stall. Both op-node and kona-node always stamp a block with its parent's timestamp plus the block time; a sequencer that stalls falls behind the wall clock and then catches up with back-to-back blocks, and the timestamps never show it. The wait checks the timestamp delta as asked, and anchors "missed slot" to the wall clock: a block is late when it is not canonical before its own timestamp plus the block time, that is before the next block is due.
- "Using the hooks upstream exposes after the handoff removal": upstream exposes no persistence hook. `TempDatabase`'s transaction hooks wrap read transactions only. What both pins expose is `NodeBuilder::with_database` with any `Database` implementation, and the persistence service's write transaction is the first thing a batch takes, so a gated database is the seam. Stated in the test's module comment.

## Seams

- `dsl.L2ELNode.AdvancedOnSchedule` / `AdvancedOnScheduleFn` with `ScheduleOpts`: holds a chain to its block schedule; the first DSL wait on block cadence.
- `dsl.EOA.DeployStorageFiller(slotsPerCall)`: a contract whose every call creates that many storage slots it has never written, for loads that must grow state.
- The workload (two senders, rounds off the test goroutine) is package-local like the crash and upgrade packages' workloads; it is the fourth copy of the shape and the follow-up to fold them into the DSL now has four inputs.

`go-code-reviewer` and `rust-code-reviewer` were both run and every finding addressed: the workload goroutine is now joined in a `t.Cleanup` so a failed schedule wait stops the load before the nodes it drives; every transaction of a round is checked, not just the last; the block time comes from the chain config rather than the test's constant, and the wait rejects a block time that is not whole seconds; the ancestor fetch is bounded and retried; the overdue arithmetic shares one boundary definition with the per-block check and has its own table test; the catch-up wait logs once per head; a block later than half a block time is logged at warning level so a CI failure shows lag climbing before the failing block. On the Rust side the batch is parked inside the real write transaction rather than before it, a timed job now spans the batch landing (the window the fork protected), the gate uses `Condvar::wait_while` and closing it returns the reopen guard, the watchdog thread that could not fire under nextest's 120s timeout and would have killed the sibling case under `cargo test` is gone, and tautological assertions were dropped.

Stacked on #23431, #23427, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23397

topPRs.title: op-reth: report subblock/sealed-block agreement from the flashblocks follower
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Prototype for the SLO-1 "agreement" indicator: does each sealed block contain exactly the transactions its subblocks promised, in order? Refs https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/core-team/issues/3202 (not closed by this PR: the dashboard panel and burn-rate alert follow in k8s once the metric has data).

**Why here.** The op-reth flashblocks follower is the only component already running on every OP Labs network that holds both sides, the subblock stream and the canonical chain, yet it never compared them: the service's canonical-block channel had no production caller, so its reconciliation path and `reth_flashblock_service_reorg_count` were dead (the counter has read 0 on every network for 30 days through 20+ leader changes a week). The websocket proxy still lives upstream in flashbots/rollup-boost and has no chain view, and `op-flashblocks-indexer` persists only tx counts, so both would need new plumbing to reach parity.

**Effect on operators.** Nodes run with `--flashblocks-url` gain the counters `reth_flashblock_service_agreement_{match,content_mismatch,ordering_mismatch,unobserved,orphaned_payloads}` and a `warn` line per mismatched block naming the block, payload id and first divergent index. The same wiring activates the follower's existing canonical-block reconciliation on every block for the first time: once canonical catches up to the stream the pending state is cleared, and a reorg clears it when no tracked variant of the block matches canonical. Please compare `stale_builds_discarded` and the `drain_followup_*` counters on a devnet follower before and after. With `--flashblocks-consensus` the check is circular (canonical blocks are built from the stream) and always reports a match.

**Design points the diff does not explain.**
- A sealed block is judged only after the stream has moved past it, and only the stream advances that frontier, so a lagging websocket delays the verdict instead of reporting a producer mismatch; a sequence joined mid-block is never judged.
- Payloads are keyed by `payload_id`, so a leadership transfer compares against the payload that sealed and counts the deposed leader's stream as `orphaned_payloads` rather than as a divergence. Orphans are expected until the handoff improves, so they should not burn the SLO budget.
- Subblocks carry `block_hash = 0`, so the reorg detector now compares a tracked block hash only when it is non-zero.

**Reviews.** `rust-code-reviewer` ran; its findings (false mismatch on mid-block join, sealed side moving the frontier, reorg detection comparing only the newest variant) are addressed. One suggestion not taken: splitting the canonical wiring into its own PR or a flag. I kept it in for the prototype so the metric has data; happy to split if the reviewer prefers. `security-review` skipped: no new input surface, the tracker consumes the payloads the service already parses. Clippy with the pinned nightly reports one pre-existing `question_mark` finding at `cache.rs:478` that also fires on `develop`; not touched here.

topPRs.title: rust: drop advisories from cargo-deny and gate PRs on it
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
`rust-deny` now runs only the bans, licenses, and sources checks. It runs on every PR and is part of `required-rust-ci`. Dependency vulnerabilities are already tracked through the Wiz scanning of our published images, so the advisory check duplicated that work in a separate place. It also paged @protocol-oncall after merge every time a new RustSec advisory landed, even when nothing upstream could fix it yet. The latest example is RUSTSEC-2026-0344 (`ruzstd`, blocked on SP1 and `backtrace`).

Without advisories, the result depends only on `Cargo.lock`, `rust/deny.toml`, and the pinned `cargo-deny` version, so the job can only fail because of a repo change. That is why it now blocks the PR that introduces a disallowed license, banned crate, or unknown source, instead of reporting it after the change lands on develop. The develop on-call ping stays as a backstop.

The `[advisories]` ignore list in `rust/deny.toml` is removed because nothing evaluates it anymore.

This makes #23364 unnecessary.

I skipped the review agents because the diff only changes CI and config scope. `cargo deny --all-features check bans licenses sources` (cargo-deny 0.19.4) passes locally on develop. I checked that the CircleCI file still parses as YAML but did not run `circleci config validate`.

Prompted by: @joshklop

This is a patch release, and its dependency requirements are identical to the version it replaces, so only the `rustls` entry in `rust/Cargo.lock` changes.

I skipped the review agents and did not build the workspace locally (the sandbox cannot build it). CI is the build check.
